searchText: And the time for discussing the consensus protocol in a productive manner was 5 years ago. Not even 2 years ago because at the time Medalla testnet was already in full swing. We’ve had this discussion in DMs: This is 1559 all over again. The time for design discussions is truly past. At some Point a feature has to ship. I’d be keen to see all this energy directed towards design though. Ethereum Classic as a hybrid PoW/PoS chain like you envision. Shards on it too, why not. A truly competing vision, executed well. Oh no just don’t touch ETC 😅😅 It’s already at its best > as a hybrid PoW/PoS chain like you envision Also I’m not sure where you are getting this info from. Never even thought about hybrid consensus as I think it’s useless. My vision is for the base (L1) layer to be as lightweight as possible, while all scaling is to be done on L2 only Also, the idea of making L2 from Ethereum base layer sounds stupid to me. L1 should always be L1 for large payments, and L2 should be used for small-value transactions only because L2s are fundamentally much less secure and less decentralized. Sounds like an entirely new chain and design to me. Go for it! > making L2 from Ethereum base layer what do you mean by that? L1 focuses on L1 things and just provides the helpful tools for L2s to thrive, but doesnt impose how L2s should do it It’s not entirely new And there is Bitcoin, which successfully implements it But no smart contracts there unfortunately By L2 in that context I mean high TPS low security/decentralization People believe in high TPS high security/decentralization utopia, but realistically it is impossible the point of a well-implemented rollup is you can still trustlessly recreate the rollup state from data available on L1, and force-exit or force-push L2 transactions. It's as close as that utopia as you can get imo I’m not very familiar with rollups, but if it’s true then it is like Bitcoin’s LN So why I hate PoS - it makes Ethereum architecture extremely hard to understand. Yet no one has clear understanding of how both chains work in detail, and I think that’s a problem A large-scale problem. You don't have to have a deep understanding of all the moving parts involved, that's why it's all getting modularized You don’t have to unless shit happens and you have to investigate what is wrong And there is a communication bottleneck that will keep things very slow There’s just no point in PoS itself as it only makes things worse. Yes it is cheaper, but it makes the system exponentially more complex depends at what level said shit happens, there's a lot of resiliency and fallbacks at every level (like client diversity to prevent one bug from one client taking the whole thing down) - core PoS spec actually aims to be as simple as possible from a technical complexity point of view Check out ETC Good PoW network destroying the environment Can always move there post merge What’s the point of creating a room for issues and then working on fixing them? because the benefits outweigh the risks/costs especially with a more ambitious long-term thinking with ethereum's aim at being self-sustainable and maximally resilient I do have high hopes for it, but unfortunately there’s none of DeFi there also stuff like encapsulated complexity is what's probably desirable, small clusters of isolated stuff of a few simple parts vs a whole mesh of interconnected moving parts which is what's done by isolating all the layers of consensus and execution and then even more with L2s etc Imo if you have two layers relying on each other then it’s systemic complexity the dependency is extremely limited tho. you get the consensus layer containing execution payload that it doesnt try to understand, and then existing battle tested code from execution clients does the rest And anyway - we can endlessly discuss this without any consensus as your all’s goal here is to shill PoS, not to come with an actual consensus well okay then lol not sure why i'd shill PoS in an ethereum R&D discord, i was just trying to provide some perspective the mining pool guy is obviously right, blockchain peaked with PoW and anything else is doomed to fail so why even try I'm a mining pool guy because I love PoW, not the other way around That's a ridiculously general statement Does TCP have a lot of systemic complexity because there's 3 other layers underneath it that all interact? tbf ETC has pretty low hashrate so that's not a major impact compared to like, cars
